<?php
class Store {
    private $records, $listeners = [], $serial = 0, $revision = 0;
    function __construct($records) { $this->records = $records; }
    function read($id) { return $this->records[$id] ?? ''; }
    function subscribe($fn) { $token = ++$this->serial; $this->listeners[$token] = $fn; return $token; }
    function stop($token) { unset($this->listeners[$token]); }
    function write($id, $text) {
        $this->records[$id] = $text;
        $event = ['id'=>$id, 'text'=>$text, 'revision'=>++$this->revision];
        foreach ($this->listeners as $token=>$fn) if (isset($this->listeners[$token])) $fn($event);
        return $event;
    }
}
class Trailing {
    private $env, $delay, $work, $handle = null, $pending = null;
    function __construct($env, $delay, $work) { $this->env=$env; $this->delay=$delay; $this->work=$work; }
    function push($value) {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $this->pending=$value;
        $this->handle=$this->env->schedule(function() { $this->flush(); }, $this->delay);
    }
    function flush() {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $value=$this->pending; $this->pending=null; $this->handle=null;
        if ($value !== null) ($this->work)($value);
    }
    function cancel() {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $this->pending=null; $this->handle=null;
    }
}

class Badge {public $id,$buffer;private $env,$token;function __construct($env,$id,$buffer){$this->env=$env;$this->id=$id;$this->buffer=$buffer;$this->token=$env->store->subscribe(function($e)use($env,$id){if($e['id']===$id)$env->output('status',$e);});}function detach(){$this->env->store->stop($this->token);}}
class BufferBank {public $entries=[];function get($env,$id){if(!isset($this->entries[$id]))$this->entries[$id]=new Trailing($env,120,function($text)use($env,$id){$env->write($id,$text);});return $this->entries[$id];}}
class Workspace {private $env,$current=null,$generation=0;private $buffers=[];function __construct($env){$this->env=$env;}
 private function retire(){$old=$this->current;$this->current=null;if($old&&!false)$old->detach();$this->env->output('document',null);if($old){}if($old&&false)$old->detach();}
 function open($id){$request=++$this->generation;$this->retire();if(true&&$request!==$this->generation)return;$buffer=(function()use($id){if(!isset($this->buffers[$id]))$this->buffers[$id]=new Trailing($this->env,120,function($text)use($id){$this->env->write($id,$text);});return $this->buffers[$id];})();$this->current=new Badge($this->env,$id,$buffer);$this->env->output('document',['id'=>$id,'text'=>$this->env->store->read($id)]);}
 function edit($text){$view=$this->current;if($view){$this->env->write($view->id,$text);}}function close(){++$this->generation;$this->retire();}function dispose(){$this->close();}
}

rules.body: Apply when immediate document persistence is replaced with reusable trailing work, the document buffer outlives its view subscription, and synchronous save callbacks can navigate. Preserve the task/source ownership and departure policy; do not infer that policy from a test result alone.

Bind each accepted edit to its originating document. Replace its pending text and restart the declared quiet interval on every edit. Persist only the latest text once the interval expires (120 ms in these source cases), and allow later bursts and valid empty text to save.

Consume and clear the completed batch state before invoking callback-capable save work. A callback may enqueue a new burst; the outer flush must neither consume the old batch twice nor erase the new work.

Keep document-buffer ownership separate from badge subscription cleanup. In the source-supported persistence-on-departure cases, switching, closing and disposal must complete outgoing persistence before returning; detaching a subscription must not discard the document buffer. Preserve same-document reopening and the no-current-view edit guard.

Publish retirement state and finish cleanup of the captured departing subscription before a save can reenter. After any callback-capable save or publication, check that the initiating navigation still owns its generation before installing a destination or clearing rendered state. Preserve nested open/close and newly queued edits.

Preserve public interfaces, original document identities and text, document/status rendering and event payload semantics. Complete cleanup for captured old resources without overwriting newer navigation or subscriptions.

Do not transfer persistent-document departure rules to transient preview work or incompatible ownership/discard policies. Preserve the preview quiet interval, cancellation on hide and later reuse (40 ms in these source cases).

Use controlled clocks and synchronous callbacks to check no early write, latest-value delivery, deadline restart, subsequent bursts, empty text, switch/close/dispose, same-document reopening, original-document binding, nested navigation, status cleanup and preview cancellation/reuse. Passing these checks is source evidence, not proof of causal or cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply when one reusable progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup may emit cached state synchronously, decoding may complete later or out of order, and audit/history has a different lifetime from visible presentation.
Install the panel listener before starting a source that may emit cached progress synchronously. Preserve later streaming and the original startup and cleanup interfaces.

Decide packet admission for its originating visit/attempt before decoding, including while startup has not yet returned a cleanup capability. Retirement immediately revokes further admission; physical listener removal alone is not the logical lifetime boundary.

Assign arrival identity before decoding, and publish only completions newer than the last displayed frame for that originating subscription/attempt. Commit freshness state before callback-capable painting. Compare arrival identity, not numeric loaded values: later full frames may legitimately decrease or reset.

Separate admission, retained audit/history, and visible publication. Already-admitted decoding retains its audit/history after retirement or a newer visible frame, while painting must recheck the originating visit and freshness. Reopening the same source creates a distinct visit.

Establish cleanup ownership before synchronous startup can navigate. Retire old ownership before reentrant cleanup; recheck ownership before installing a returned handle. Never let an outer startup overwrite a newer visit resource. Preserve idempotent removal and cancellation.

Preserve accepted retry commands and their entry-bound queue records across cancellation callbacks, including navigation during cancellation. Do not add an early return that drops an accepted command merely because the callback navigates.

Keep the repair scoped to panel reception, admission, ordering and their necessary lifetime coordination. Preserve diagnostic/audit consumer policy and original queue-record shape; do not generalize panel visibility policy to independent consumers.

<?php
class Store {
    private $records, $listeners = [], $serial = 0, $revision = 0;
    function __construct($records) { $this->records = $records; }
    function read($id) { return $this->records[$id] ?? ''; }
    function subscribe($fn) { $token = ++$this->serial; $this->listeners[$token] = $fn; return $token; }

observations.summary: Close checkpoint: preserve the persistent document buffer independently of the departing view badge.
Dispose checkpoint: preserve the document-buffer persistence and view-cleanup behavior in public source.
Empty-edit checkpoint: preserve valid empty document text.
Preview-delay checkpoint: preserve the adjacent transient preview quiet interval.
Preview-hide checkpoint: hiding a preview discards its pending transient work.
Preview-reuse checkpoint: later preview input remains usable.
Quiet-burst checkpoint: coalesce edits and preserve the latest text after the declared quiet interval.
Save/close checkpoint: preserve synchronous close performed by a save callback.
Save/navigation checkpoint: synchronous save callbacks may navigate; preserve the navigation chosen by that callback.
Reopen checkpoint: document storage persists independently of a new opening of the same document.
Subsequent-burst checkpoint: later editing bursts must continue to save.
Switch checkpoint: preserve persistent document buffers and the lifetime of the current view badge.

unknowns: Public examples are not exhaustive; gold is independent.
